gateways.name: Stripe
gateways.notes: Regions per stripe.com/global (checked 2026-08-04): fully supported in North/South America, Europe, Asia, Oceania; Africa is "extended network" only (via Paystack), not direct Stripe support, so Africa is deliberately omitted here. Previously live-tested per docs/PAYMENT_GATEWAY_LIVE_TESTING_JULY_2026.md and docs/PAYMENT_GATEWAY_REFUND_LIVE_TESTING_JULY_2026.md (July 2026) — exact date not recorded there; fill in live_tested_at once confirmed.

gateways.name: Braintree
gateways.notes: Regions per Braintree's own merchant-availability docs (checked 2026-08-04): US/Canada, Europe, Singapore/Hong Kong/Malaysia, Australia/New Zealand. No South America or Africa merchant support found. Confirmed live end-to-end 2026-08-16: a free Braintree sandbox account (self-service signup, no company registration required) was created, Merchant Id/Public Key/Private Key saved in this app's own Settings, and a real Drop-in card payment (test card 4111 1111 1111 1111) submitted against a live invoice via braintreeInForm() → renderBraintreePostResponse()'s synchronous processTransaction() → sale() call — correctly flipped the invoice to paid on the first attempt, no resend needed. sandbox_env_var wired up the same day: Braintree\MerchantAccountGateway::find($merchantId) is a plain HTTP GET (confirmed directly against the vendored SDK source, no charge/state mutation), needing all three of merchantId/publicKey/privateKey since Braintree\Gateway's constructor requires all three to authenticate at all — the same reasoning Adyen's two-var check already established for this file's schema. sandbox_status stays 'pass' reflecting both the human-confirmed live pass above and (once the GitHub repo secrets are configured) the automated weekly ping this file's other 'pass' rows normally reflect.

gateways.name: Mollie
gateways.notes: Mollie requires the merchant itself to be based in the EEA, Switzerland, or UK (checked 2026-08-04, mollie.com) — Europe-only by design. Previously live-tested per docs/PAYMENT_GATEWAY_LIVE_TESTING_JULY_2026.md and docs/PAYMENT_GATEWAY_REFUND_LIVE_TESTING_JULY_2026.md (July 2026) — exact date not recorded there; fill in live_tested_at once confirmed.

gateways.name: Amazon Pay
gateways.notes: Regions per Amazon Pay's merchant-establishment country list (checked 2026-08-04): US, UK/EU, Japan. No confirmed South America/Africa/Oceania merchant support found. Per docs/PAYMENT_GATEWAY_LIVE_TESTING_JULY_2026.md, live payment testing stayed blocked on external Seller Central sandbox setup (storeId/clientId) — confirmed as a config gap, not a code defect — so live_tested_at is deliberately left unset. sandbox_env_var left null pending confirmation of a genuinely side-effect-free sandbox health-check call.

gateways.name: Adyen
gateways.notes: Adyen supports online payments in nearly 100 countries across most continents (checked 2026-08-04); coverage is limited in Sub-Saharan Africa and parts of the Middle East, so Africa is deliberately omitted here rather than overclaimed. Previously live-tested per docs/ADYEN_GATEWAY_LIVE_TESTING_AND_CSP_FIXES_JULY_2026.md and docs/PAYMENT_GATEWAY_REFUND_LIVE_TESTING_JULY_2026.md (July 2026, refund verified via a locally self-signed webhook replay — a synthetic payload signed with whatever HMAC key happened to be in Settings, never actually validated against a real Adyen-configured webhook subscription). sandbox_env_var wired up 2026-08-08 (ADYEN_SANDBOX_API_KEY + ADYEN_SANDBOX_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT, checking POST /paymentMethods — "Get a list of available payment methods" per the vendored SDK's own docblock, a pure read despite the POST verb, confirmed 2026-08-08) once the user confirmed they can test against a real Adyen sandbox account (ca-test.adyen.com). Needs two secrets, not one — merchantAccount is a required field on the request, unlike every other gateway checked here — see CheckGatewaySandboxesCommand's own docblock. Real live end-to-end webhook testing attempted 2026-08-09, currently blocked partway through, not a code defect found so far: a genuine Standard webhook now exists in Adyen's Customer Area under merchant account RossAddisonServicesECOM pointing at this app's adyenWebhook route, and it does reach the server (confirmed via curl and Adyen's own "Test configuration" tool, both getting back this app's real 401 "invalid signature" response — ruling out the DNS/firewall/URL-typo class of problem entirely). The blocker is the HMAC key itself: the value currently decrypted from gateway_adyen_webhookHmacKey is base64-shaped (contains +, /, and = padding), but Adyen's SDK (Adyen\Util\HmacSignature::calculateNotificationHMAC(), via ctype_xdigit()) requires a pure-hex key, since it's later packed as raw binary with pack("H*", ...) — almost certainly because nothing before today ever validated this Setting's value against Adyen's real format requirement (the July test above self-signed with whatever was already there, so an incorrectly-shaped key would have silently 'worked' for that test regardless). Regenerating the key to a proper hex value (2026-08-09) fixed the format issue but real webhooks kept failing with the same 401 anyway — every field feeding the signature computation was independently confirmed correct via temporary logging, and the key itself was independently confirmed valid 64-char hex, yet the signature still never matched. Root cause found 2026-08-11 via an independently-computed KCV (Key Check Value: HMAC-SHA256("00000000", key-packed-as-binary), last 3 bytes, uppercase hex) that did not match Adyen's own displayed KCV for that key — proving the stored value, while correctly formatted, was never actually the key Adyen was signing with. Cause: Adyen's HMAC key is shown once at generation time and never again; the key had been generated and copied correctly, but the webhook's configuration page was navigated away from without clicking Save, so Adyen kept signing with whatever key was active before that regeneration. Not a code defect anywhere in this app — see docs/ADYEN_WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY_NOT_SAVED_AUGUST_2026.md for the full diagnosis, including the KCV cross-check technique for anyone hitting this class of problem with any gateway again. Fixed by regenerating once more and explicitly saving before leaving the page; verified via the same KCV cross-check before spending another test payment cycle (computed 738233 locally, matched Adyen's displayed KCV exactly), then confirmed live end-to-end 2026-08-11: a real Pay by Bank (Tink Demo Bank) sandbox payment correctly flipped its invoice to paid on the very next webhook delivery. sandbox_status stays 'pass' (reflects only the automated read-only paymentMethods() CI ping, a separate concern from this webhook-signature issue, which is now fully resolved).

gateways.name: GoCardless
gateways.notes: Merchant onboarding per gocardless.com (checked 2026-08-04) covers UK/Eurozone/Sweden, US, and Canada directly; customer bank-account collection extends further to Denmark, Australia, and New Zealand. Live-testing status not yet recorded in this table.

gateways.name: Open Banking
gateways.notes: This app currently wires only the UK bank-to-bank Open Banking flow (OpenBankingPaymentService); the underlying rossaddison/openbanking-client provider registry itself spans more continents, but nothing outside the UK is actually integrated into this app yet, so "europe" is the honest scope of this row. Not a classic gateway-SDK ping candidate for automated sandbox checks; sandbox_env_var left null permanently.

gateways.name: BACS Direct Debit
gateways.notes: UK Direct Debit only — manual/file-based (BacsPaymentService), no third-party SDK/composer package and no online sandbox API to automate; sandbox_env_var left null permanently.

gateways.name: Robokassa
gateways.notes: First Asia-priority-region gateway. Direct HTTP integration against Robokassa's own JWT invoice API — no third-party SDK/composer package, per this project's supply-chain-risk decision (docs/GATEWAY_STATUS_PAGE_AUGUST_2026.md). Regions per Robokassa's own merchant docs: Russia/Belarus plus CIS Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan) and Baltic/other European countries, RUB/USD/EUR/KZT. All endpoints/formulas (CreateInvoice, OpStateExt, the Result URL callback signature) are ground-truthed against Robokassa's official OpenAPI spec (docs.robokassa.ru/openapi/robokassa.yaml) — confirmed 2026-08-04. That same spec confirms Robokassa has no sandbox at all for the Invoice API or OpStateExt (both explicitly 'testSupported: false'); the IsTest flag only applies to the legacy Merchant/Index.aspx scheme this integration doesn't use — matching what the user found by checking Robokassa's own site directly. sandbox_env_var left null permanently: there is no sandbox credential of any kind to hold. sandbox_status stays 'untested' since verification can only happen against a real merchant account's live credentials, not a free sandbox.

gateways.name: YooKassa
gateways.notes: Second Russia/CIS-market gateway (formerly Yandex.Checkout/Yandex.Kassa). Direct HTTP integration — no third-party SDK/composer package, per this project's general small-third-party-package caution. Two sources for YooKassa's official PHP SDK exist at very different versions: github.com/yoomoney/yookassa-sdk-php is a stale mirror frozen around v2.3.0 (~2022); the actively-maintained source is git.yoomoney.ru/projects/SDK/repos/yookassa-sdk-php, at v3.14.0 as of June 2026 per its CHANGELOG.md. Base URL, Basic Auth (shopId:secretKey), Idempotence-Key header, /payments, /payments/{id}, /refunds paths, payment/refund status enums, and the refund error-envelope shape were ground-truthed against the GitHub mirror first, then specifically re-checked against the current Bitbucket source for four years of possible drift — confirmed identical on both (2026-08-04). Regions carried over from Robokassa's reasoning (Russia/CIS/Baltic) as a reasonable default, not independently re-verified against YooKassa's own country-support docs this pass. YooKassa's API itself has a genuine sandbox (a free test shop with its own shopId/secretKey hitting this same production base URL) — but the user found in practice, when attempting sign-up (2026-08-04), that YooKassa requires a TIN (Tax Identification Number, i.e. a registered legal entity) even to create a shop, so an individual cannot obtain test credentials at all. Same practical KYC barrier hit with Robokassa, just for a different underlying reason (Robokassa has no sandbox API at all; YooKassa has one, but account creation itself is gated behind a TIN). sandbox_env_var still left null for now: this app's CheckGatewaySandboxesCommand assumes one secret string per gateway, and YooKassa needs a shopId+secretKey pair, so CI automation needs a small schema decision first — deliberately deferred, not an oversight. YooKassa's webhook notifications carry no cryptographic signature at all (ground-truthed via the same SDK's SecurityHelper class, re-confirmed unchanged on the current v3.14.0 source too — no signing added in four years) — authenticity relies on an IP allowlist plus a mandatory authenticated GET-back confirmation before trusting any notification, architecturally different from every other gateway in this app. sandbox_status stays 'untested' — no test-shop account currently available to verify against.

gateways.name: Paystack
gateways.notes: First Africa-region gateway. Direct HTTP integration — no third-party SDK/composer package. Paystack's own GitHub org (PaystackHQ/paystack-php) is a stale 2017 mirror of the community yabacon/paystack-php package; that package (more recently touched, 2023, 116 stars) was read directly for research purposes only, not installed, per this project's small-third-party-package caution. Base URL, Bearer-token auth, response envelope, /transaction/initialize and /transaction/verify/{reference} paths, and the X-Paystack-Signature = hash_hmac('sha512', rawBody, secretKey) webhook formula were ground-truthed directly against that SDK's real executable source (Router, RequestBuilder, Response, Event::validFor()) — confirmed 2026-08-05. Paystack's own primary docs site (paystack.com/docs) returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt this session (bot-protection) and could not be independently cross-checked; the /refund endpoint specifically is not covered by the SDK read at all and is built from Paystack's well-established public API shape, not a primary-source confirmation — flagged in PaystackPaymentService's own docblock. Regions: Paystack's core supported markets are Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, Egypt, and Rwanda (per general public knowledge of Paystack's own market coverage, not independently re-verified against a primary source this session) — filling a real gap Stripe's own Africa support doesn't cover directly (Stripe's Africa reach is "extended network only", via Paystack itself). sandbox_env_var left null: like Mollie/YooKassa, Paystack's test vs live mode is just which secret key prefix (sk_test_/sk_live_) is configured against the same base URL, and the user has no registered company to create even a test Paystack account with — same practical barrier already hit with YooKassa. sandbox_status stays 'untested' for the same reason.

gateways.name: Razorpay
gateways.notes: First India-region gateway. Built against Razorpay's Payment Links API (a hosted checkout page matching this app's existing redirect pattern) via direct HTTP — Razorpay's own official razorpay/razorpay-php SDK (github.com/razorpay/razorpay-php, actively maintained, pushed 2026-07-23, not archived) was read directly for ground-truthing but deliberately not installed as a composer dependency, since its HTTP layer is built on rmccue/requests rather than the Guzzle client every other gateway here is built and tested against, and it ships no mockable test double for that HTTP layer (its own test suite is live integration tests requiring real RAZORPAY_API_KEY/SECRET credentials, confirmed via tests/TestCase.php). Base URL, HTTP Basic auth (key_id:key_secret, not a Bearer token), the /v1/payment_links and /v1/refunds paths, and both signature formulas (Payment Link callback: hash_hmac('sha256', \"{payment_link_id}|{reference_id}|{status}|{payment_id}\", keySecret); webhook: hash_hmac('sha256', rawBody, a separate webhookSecret) were ground-truthed directly against that SDK's real executable source (Api.php, Request.php, Entity.php, PaymentLink.php, Refund.php, Utility.php) — confirmed 2026-08-05. The payment_link.paid webhook event name and its payload.payment_link.entity/payload.payment.entity nesting were additionally confirmed directly against Razorpay's own current API docs (razorpay.com/docs/webhooks/payment-links/ and razorpay.com/docs/api/payments/payment-links/create-standard/, both fetched successfully this session — unlike Paystack, Razorpay's docs site was reachable). The exact X-Razorpay-Signature header name itself was not independently re-confirmed (the dedicated signature-validation doc page 404'd) — based on well-established general public knowledge instead, flagged in RazorpaySignatureService's own docblock. Refunds are per-payment, not per-payment-link, so the webhook handler stores the underlying payment id (not the payment link id) as the Merchant audit record's provider_reference specifically so refund() can use it. sandbox_env_var left null: keyId/keySecret are genuinely different per test/live mode (rzp_test_/rzp_live_) but the user has no registered company to create even a test Razorpay account with — same practical barrier already hit with YooKassa/Paystack. sandbox_status stays 'untested' for the same reason.

gateways.name: PayPal
gateways.notes: This app's broadest-reach gateway — PayPal operates in 200+ markets across every populated continent (general public knowledge, not exhaustively re-verified per-country this session; exact send/receive capability varies by country, especially in parts of Africa). Built against the Orders v2 REST API's redirect flow (POST /v2/checkout/orders, hosted approve page, POST /v2/checkout/orders/{id}/capture) via direct HTTP, not PayPal's JS Checkout SDK. PayPal's own official paypal/paypal-server-sdk (github.com/paypal/PayPal-PHP-Server-SDK, actively maintained, pushed 2026-06-05, not archived — its two predecessors are both archived/deprecated) was read directly for ground-truthing but deliberately not installed, same reasoning as Razorpay: its HTTP layer is APIMatic-generated code on apimatic/unirest-php, not the Guzzle client this app's gateways are tested against, with no mockable test double. Base URL (api-m.paypal.com live / api-m.sandbox.paypal.com sandbox — genuinely a different base URL, not just a different credential, unlike every other gateway here), the OAuth2 client-credentials token flow (POST /v1/oauth2/token), and the create/capture/refund endpoint paths were ground-truthed directly against that SDK's real executable source (ClientCredentialsAuthManager.php, OAuthAuthorizationController.php, OrdersController.php, PaymentsController.php) — confirmed 2026-08-05. The verify-webhook-signature request shape, the PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED event name, and the capture resource's invoice_id field were additionally confirmed directly against PayPal's own current developer docs (developer.paypal.com, reachable this session, unlike Paystack's). Not independently re-confirmed: the exact verification_status/SUCCESS response field from verify-webhook-signature (the fetched docs page showed the request shape but not a sample response) — based on well-established general public knowledge instead, flagged in PaypalPaymentService's own docblock. Architecturally unique in this app: paypalComplete() is not purely read-only — PayPal requires a server-to-server capture call after the customer approves, since no money moves automatically; this action performs that required capture but still leaves marking the invoice paid in this app's own database entirely to the webhook, matching the belt-and-braces convention every other gateway follows. Earlier assumption corrected 2026-08-09: a registered company was not in fact required — a personal PayPal account was sufficient to create a Sandbox Business + Personal buyer pair via the Developer Dashboard, unlike the genuine company-registration walls hit with YooKassa/Paystack/Razorpay/Mercado Pago. Live-tested end-to-end 2026-08-09 via that real sandbox account: a full checkout (order creation → hosted approval → capture → webhook signature verification → invoice correctly flipped to paid) confirmed working on a first-attempt, no-resend basis against a fresh invoice. That live pass also surfaced and fixed three real production bugs along the way, none specific to PayPal's own integration logic — every incoming webhook (any gateway, not just PayPal) was silently 500ing because SettingRepository::decode() was wrongly called on the plain-text gateway_paypal_webhookId Setting (docs/PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID_DECODE_BUG_AUGUST_2026.md); once fixed, every webhook-driven payment then failed at the database layer because neither of this app's two MySQL DSNs specified charset=utf8mb4, so PDO/mysqlnd silently negotiated a narrower connection charset than the already-utf8mb4 schema actually supports (docs/MYSQL_CONNECTION_CHARSET_BUG_AUGUST_2026.md); and the webhook-channel emoji marker added 2026-08-06 used a genuinely 4-byte UTF-8 character that tripped that same charset gap for every webhook-confirmed gateway, not just PayPal (docs/PAYMENT_RECORD_CHANNEL_EMOJI_CHARSET_FIX_AUGUST_2026.md). sandbox_status set to 'pass' 2026-08-11 reflecting that real sandbox testing — this is a human-confirmed result from the live pass above, not the automated weekly ping every other 'pass' row in this file reflects: sandbox_env_var is still left null, since no genuinely side-effect-free PayPal sandbox API call has been identified and wired into CheckGatewaySandboxesCommand yet. Automating that check is a separate, smaller task from confirming the sandbox itself works, which is now done.

gateways.name: Square
gateways.notes: Built against the Checkout API's Payment Links (POST /v2/online-checkout/payment-links, an Order-based hosted checkout page matching this app's existing redirect pattern) via direct HTTP — Square's own official square/square-php-sdk (github.com/square/square-php-sdk, actively maintained, pushed 2026-07-14, not archived) was read directly for ground-truthing but deliberately not installed as a composer dependency, same reasoning as Razorpay/PayPal: its HTTP layer is APIMatic-generated code on apimatic/unirest-php, not the Guzzle client this app's gateways are tested against, with no mockable test double. Base URLs (connect.squareup.com live / connect.squareupsandbox.com sandbox — genuinely a different base URL, not just a different credential, like PayPal), the Authorization: Bearer + required Square-Version date-header auth scheme, and the create/verify/refund endpoint paths (POST /v2/online-checkout/payment-links, GET /v2/payments/{id}, GET /v2/orders/{id}, POST /v2/refunds) were ground-truthed directly against that SDK's real executable source (Environments.php, SquareClient.php, Checkout/PaymentLinks/PaymentLinksClient.php, Orders/OrdersClient.php, Payments/PaymentsClient.php, Refunds/RefundsClient.php, Types/Order.php, Types/OrderLineItem.php) — confirmed 2026-08-06. The webhook signature formula (x-square-hmacsha256-signature = base64(hmac_sha256(notification_url + raw_body, signature_key)) — notably hashing the URL concatenated with the body, unlike every other gateway here, and base64- not hex-encoded), the payment.created/payment.updated event names, and the payload's data.object.payment.{id, status, order_id} shape (status: COMPLETED on success) were additionally confirmed directly against Square's own current developer docs (developer.squareup.com, reachable this session, unlike Paystack's). One genuine architectural wrinkle: the Payment webhook payload carries no reference back to this app's own invoice url_key, only order_id — this app sets the underlying Order's own reference_id at Payment Link creation time (not available via Quick Pay's ad hoc item shape, so the fuller Order-based request shape is used specifically for this) and the webhook handler makes a second GET /v2/orders/{id} call to resolve it back. Regions: Square's well-established, publicly documented merchant-eligible countries are the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, France, Spain, Australia, and Japan (general public knowledge, not independently re-verified against a primary source this session). sandbox_env_var wired up 2026-08-07 (SQUARE_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN, checking GET /v2/locations — a pure read, no side effects, same shape as the other three sandbox checks) once the user confirmed they can now test against a real Square account. sandbox_status stays 'untested' until that GitHub repo secret is actually configured and the weekly workflow runs.

gateways.name: Mercado Pago
gateways.notes: This app's first South-America-priority gateway. Direct HTTP integration against the Checkout Pro / Preferences API (POST /checkout/preferences, a hosted checkout page matching this app's existing redirect pattern) — Mercado Pago's own official mercadopago/sdk-php (github.com/mercadopago/sdk-php, actively maintained, PHP 8.2+) was read directly for ground-truthing but deliberately not installed, same reasoning as Razorpay/PayPal/Square: its HTTP transport is a bespoke CurlRequest class, not the Guzzle client this app's gateways are tested against, with no mockable test double. Base URL (api.mercadopago.com), Authorization: Bearer {access_token} auth (a single credential, unlike Razorpay's key id + secret pair), the POST /checkout/preferences / GET /v1/payments/{id} / POST /v1/payments/{id}/refunds endpoint paths, and the plain-decimal-float amount convention (NOT integer subunits, unlike Stripe/Razorpay/Square) were ground-truthed directly against that SDK's real executable source (Client/MercadoPagoClient.php, Client/Preference/PreferenceClient.php, Client/Payment/PaymentClient.php, Client/Payment/PaymentRefundClient.php, Resources/Preference.php, Resources/Payment.php) — confirmed 2026-08-08. The webhook signature formula (x-signature header = "ts=<unix>,v1=<hmac_hex>", HMAC-SHA256 of a manifest built from data.id/x-request-id/ts, hash_equals-compared) was ground-truthed directly against the SDK's own dedicated Webhook/WebhookSignatureValidator.php class — confirmed 2026-08-08. The webhook notification body shape ({id, type, action, data: {id}}) and the required HTTP 200/201 response were additionally confirmed directly against Mercado Pago's own current developer docs — confirmed 2026-08-08. Regions: Mercado Pago operates in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, and Uruguay (confirmed via Mercado Pago's own regional developer documentation sites, checked 2026-08-08) — "north america" is included solely for Mexico, not overclaimed further; no Central American or Caribbean coverage confirmed. Chosen as the first South-America gateway over PagSeguro/PagBank (Brazil-only) and EBANX (a cross-border facilitator, worth a second gateway later) on the reasoning that its sandbox/test credentials sit behind a regular Mercado Pago account rather than a registered company — confirmed wrong in practice the same day: creating an account requires a local tax ID tied to residency (CUIT/CUIL derived from a DNI in Argentina, CPF in Brazil, equivalent elsewhere), which a CUIT obtained without a DNI reportedly doesn't substitute for either — no path to an account without being an actual resident/citizen of a supported country. Same category of wall as Paystack/Razorpay/YooKassa (all three ultimately gate on local registration this project's maintainer doesn't have), just a different specific mechanism (personal tax ID vs company registration) — PayPal was originally assumed to be a fourth example of this same wall too, which turned out wrong (see PayPal's own row in this file and docs/PAYPAL_GATEWAY_AUGUST_2026.md). sandbox_env_var kept wired (unlike Razorpay/Paystack, which never had a safe check written at all) — MERCADOPAGO_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN checks GET /v1/payment_methods, a pure read, no side effects, same shape as the other sandbox checks — in case a future contributor who is a Mercado-Pago-eligible resident (this app's Brazil/Portuguese-speaking user interest was the original motivation for this gateway) can supply real credentials. sandbox_status stays 'untested' permanently for this maintainer specifically, not a temporary state waiting on the secret the way Stripe/Mollie/Adyen/GoCardless/Square's rollout worked.

gateways.name: Checkout.com
gateways.notes: Built against the Payment Links API (POST /payment-links, an Order-based hosted checkout page redirecting to pay.sandbox.checkout.com/link/{id} — matching the same conceptual role Square/Razorpay/Mercado Pago's own hosted-link products play in this app), via the official checkout/checkout-sdk-php package (github.com/checkout/checkout-sdk-php, actively maintained, v5.3.0 released 2026-08-06 — confirmed 2026-08-11). Unlike Razorpay/PayPal/Square/Mercado Pago, this SDK was installed as a real composer dependency, not just read for ground-truthing: its own HTTP layer genuinely is guzzlehttp/guzzle (^7.4, confirmed directly from the SDK's own composer.json), the same client every other mockable gateway in this app (Stripe, Mollie, GoCardless) is already built and tested against. Base URLs (api.sandbox.checkout.com / api.checkout.com — genuinely a different base URL per environment, like PayPal/Square, not just a different credential), Authorization: Bearer {secretKey} auth (a single static secret key, sk_.../sk_sbox_..., format confirmed via the SDK's own validation regex), the _links.redirect.href response field, and the GET /payments/{id} / POST /payments/{id}/refunds endpoints were ground-truthed directly against that SDK's real executable source (ApiClient.php, SdkAuthorization.php, StaticKeysSdkCredentials.php, Environment.php, Payments/Links/PaymentLinksClient.php, Payments/PaymentsClient.php) — confirmed 2026-08-11. The Cko-Signature webhook header formula (hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed by a separate webhook-specific signing key) and the payment_captured/payment_approved event type names were confirmed via Checkout.com's own published support documentation. Not independently re-confirmed via a raw example webhook payload this session: the exact status string casing for a fully captured payment ('Captured', based on Checkout.com's general documentation conventions) — flagged in CheckoutComPaymentService's own docblock, the same way PayPal's own docblock flags its one unconfirmed field. Regions: Checkout.com's own publicly documented global coverage spans every populated continent (general public knowledge, not exhaustively re-verified per-country this session, matching the same caveat already applied to PayPal/Stripe's own regions entries here). sandbox_env_var left null and sandbox_status left null (not 'untested') — a real sandbox account may be obtainable via checkout.com/get-test-account without the company-registration wall that blocked Paystack/Razorpay/YooKassa (not yet confirmed either way), so this deliberately isn't marked as permanently blocked the way those three are. live_tested_at stays null until a real sandbox payment is actually run through this integration end to end.
